newsitem.title: USA: Ill. moves to consolidate all incinerator lawsuits.
newsitem.headline: Ill. moves to consolidate all incinerator lawsuits.

text.p: Attorneys representing Illinois officials in lawsuits related to incinerator funding have filed a motion with the state's supreme court to consolidate all three lawsuits.

Rick Redmond, a Chicago attorney representing the state, said Tuesday a motion was filed Friday to move a lawsuit pending in Madison County Circuit Court to Cook County Circuit Court, where two other incinerator lawsuits have already been consolidated for pre-trial purposes.
Redmond said all three lawsuits had "substantial similarities" and that it would be more efficient to handle them in a single court.
An attorney representing Polsky Energy Corp, which brought the lawsuit in Madison County, was not available for comment.
Redmond said that all three plaintiffs will have an opportunity to object to the state's motion if they choose.

Meanwhile, the two other lawsuits filed by developers of waste-to-energy incinerators in Robbins, Ford Heights and Fulton may begin to have oral arguments on motions in their cases as early as April, attorneys said.
The two lawsuits, filed by Foster Wheeler Corp and CGE Ford Heights and CGE Fulton, were consolidated last month.

All three lawsuits contested the legality of a 1996 Illinois law that repealed a state subsidy for incinerators. Nearly $500 million of unrated, tax-exempt debt that was largely dependent on the subsidy was sold to finance the projects.
